title: Highest-Protein Legumes: Ranking per 100 Grams and Serving

seo.title: Highest-Protein Legumes: Cooked Ranking
seo.meta_description: Compare cooked soybeans, lupini beans, lentils, chickpeas and beans by protein per 100 grams and realistic serving.
seo.search_intent: Compare cooked legumes by protein content.

excerpt: Cooked mature soybeans lead at about 18.2 g protein per 100 g, with lupini beans around 15.6 g. Lentils, chickpeas and common beans cluster near 8–9 g.
content_html:
Legume protein looks very different depending on whether the food is dry or cooked. For what actually reaches the plate, cooked and drained values are the most useful comparison.

Cooked legume ranking

LegumeProtein/100 g
Mature soybeans18.2 g
Lupini beans15.6 g
Lentils9.0 g
Black/pinto beans~8.9 g
Chickpeas8.9 g
Kidney beans~8.7 g
Green peas~5.4 g

Soybeans

Cooked mature soybeans provide about 18.2 g protein/100 g, roughly twice the 9 g in cooked lentils. A 1-cup serving around 170 g supplies about 31 g protein.

Soybeans are also higher in fat and calories: roughly 170 calories/100 g compared with 116 for cooked lentils.

Lupini beans

Cooked lupini beans are around 15.6 g/100 g. In the U.S. they are often sold brined, so sodium can be high; rinsing removes some surface brine.

Lentils, chickpeas and beans

These are tightly grouped around 8.7–9.0 g protein/100 g. A 1-cup serving near 200 g provides roughly 18 g from lentils, 18 g from chickpeas and 17–18 g from many common beans.

Dry vs cooked

Dry lentils contain about 24.6 g protein/100 g compared with 9.0 g after cooking. Their water content rises from roughly 8% to about 70%, spreading the protein across much more weight.

Canned beans

Canned beans are already hydrated and cooked, so their composition is much closer to cooked beans than dry beans. Draining and rinsing can reduce sodium from the packing liquid.

What about peanuts?

Peanuts are botanically legumes and contain about 25.8 g protein/100 g, higher than cooked soybeans. But they are eaten dry like nuts and contain roughly 49 g fat and more than 560 calories/100 g, making them nutritionally very different from a bowl of beans.

Protein by serving

LegumeServingProtein
Cooked soybeans1 cup / ~170 g31 g
Lupini beans1 cup / ~166 g~26 g
Lentils1 cup / ~200 g18 g
Chickpeas1 cup / ~200 g~18 g
Black beans1 cup / ~172 g~15 g

Protein plus fiber

One cup of cooked lentils provides about 18 g protein and roughly 15–16 g fiber. An equivalent 200 g weight of chicken breast provides more than 60 g protein but no fiber. The foods serve different nutritional roles.

Bottom line

Soybeans and lupini beans are the most protein-dense cooked legumes. Lentils, chickpeas and common beans are much closer together and all make substantial contributions in a normal serving while providing plenty of fiber.

Sources

Food values come from USDA FoodData Central.

faq.question: Which legume has the most protein?
faq.answer: Among cooked legumes, mature soybeans are about 18.2 g/100 g and lupini beans about 15.6 g/100 g.

faq.question: Do lentils have more protein than chickpeas?
faq.answer: Only slightly in common cooked entries: about 9.0 versus 8.9 g/100 g.

faq.question: Why do dry lentils show so much more protein?
faq.answer: They contain far less water. Cooking increases water content and weight, lowering protein concentration per 100 g.
